To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The use of wheat straw as a binder in rice husk particleboards improved the mechanical properties and water resistance of the composites.
the addition of silane and/or MAPP improved the interfacial ad-hesion and the mechanical properties of polypropylene/rice husk composites.
the addition of coupling agent and compatibilizer can improve the interfacial properties of rice husk/polypropylene composites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new composite materials using agricultural residues as reinforcing materials in order to reduce the environmental impact of wood processing.
two types of composite boards: (i) particleboards made of agricultural fibers (wheat straw, rice husk) with pMDI as a binder and (ii) composites of rice-husk and polypropylene.
the development of new composites of rice-husk and wheat-straw fibers and polymeric materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the application of agricultural fibres for making particleboards is feasible and that the use of coupling agents and compatibilisers is effective in improving the interfacial adhesions between polypropylene matrix and rice husk fillers.
the combination of silane coupling agent and MAPP as a compatibilizer is effective in improving inter- facial adhesion between polymeric matrices and agricultural fibers.
the combination of 1 wt.% silane with 1 wt.% MAPP was effective in improving the interfacial adhesions of the composites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of agricultural residues as a filler in polymer matrices has the potential for producing environmentally benign materials.
the use of silane as coupling agents and MAPP as compatibilisers can be used to produce composites with better mechanical properties.
the use of silane and/or MAPP as a coupling agent in rice husk/polypropylene composites was effective in improving mechanical properties and interface morphology of com-posites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of agricultural residues in the manufacture of composites is a promising alternative to the use of synthetic materials.
the application of agricultural fibers to produce composites with polypropylene can be improved by using coupling agent and compatibiliser.

the application of agricultural fibers to produce composites is feasible and the use of agricultural fibers in composites is an environmentally friendly approach to reduce the use of synthetic fibers and reduce the environmental impact of composites.
